theme.title: Warriors, Cavs and Raptors
theme.subtitle: The 2018 and 2019 Finals
theme.recap: LeBron James scored 51 in a 2018 loss; a year later Toronto ended Golden State's run.

questions.prompt: LeBron James scored the most points ever in a Finals loss in Game 1 of 2018. How many?
questions.context: 2018 NBA Finals · Game 1 · at Golden State

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: LeBron James scored 51 points in Game 1, the fifth-highest point total for an NBA Finals game and the most in a loss

funFacts.text: J. R. Smith grabbed an offensive rebound with the game tied but ran toward midcourt instead of shooting.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: dribbled the ball towards half court rather than taking a final shot

funFacts.text: LeBron played the remainder of the Finals with a bruised hand after punching a whiteboard in frustration.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: suffering a bone contusion in his hand that he kept private for the rest of the series

funFacts.text: Klay Thompson returned to the opener after hurting his leg in the first quarter.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: suffered a leg injury in the first quarter, but returned in the second quarter

questions.prompt: How many threes did Stephen Curry make in Game 2 of the 2018 Finals?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: set an NBA Finals record in Game 2 with nine three-point field goals

funFacts.text: Golden State increased its defensive double-teaming of LeBron after his enormous opening performance.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors employed more double teams against James in Game 2

funFacts.text: J. R. Smith struggled from the floor, with both of his field goals coming early in the night.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Smith struggled for Cleveland, shooting 2-for-9 (22.2%) with both baskets coming in the first quarter

funFacts.text: Kevin Durant contributed rebounds and playmaking alongside Curry, making Golden State's offense tougher to stop.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Warriors got 26 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists from Kevin Durant

questions.prompt: Golden State opened the second half of Game 2 of the 2019 Finals with how many unanswered points?
questions.note: 18, the most to start a half in Finals history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors' 18 unanswered points to begin the second half were the most in NBA Finals history to start a half.

funFacts.text: Klay Thompson's night ended after he landed awkwardly while attempting a three and injured his hamstring.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Thompson left the game in the fourth quarter with a left hamstring injury

funFacts.text: Andre Iguodala hit a late outside shot to prevent Toronto's comeback from forcing another ending.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Iguodala cemented the win with a three-pointer with 5.9 seconds remaining

funFacts.text: DeMarcus Cousins made a rare Finals start and added rebounds and assists after returning from injury.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Cousins, who was moved into the starting lineup, had 11 points, 10 rebounds and six assists

questions.prompt: Pascal Siakam shot 14 of 17 in Game 1 of the 2019 Finals. How many points did he score?
questions.context: 2019 NBA Finals · Game 1 · vs Golden State

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Pascal Siakam scored a playoff career-high 32 points on 14-of-17 shooting

funFacts.text: The Raptors hosted the first NBA Finals contest ever played outside the United States.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the first-ever NBA Finals game played outside the United States

funFacts.text: Draymond Green logged a triple-double in the opener, but his Warriors still fell behind in the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Draymond Green had a triple-double with 10 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists

funFacts.text: Kevin Durant traveled to Toronto but remained on the sideline while recovering from a calf injury.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Durant, the MVP of the last two NBA Finals, traveled with the team to Toronto, but remained sidelined

questions.prompt: Golden State made what was then the second-most threes in a Finals game, in Game 5 of 2019. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Golden State made 20 three-pointers, the second most in NBA Finals history behind Cleveland's 24

funFacts.text: Durant returned in the road elimination game but suffered a serious Achilles injury shortly afterward.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: he was lost for the game two minutes into the second quarter

funFacts.text: Curry and Thompson combined for consecutive late threes to keep Golden State alive for another game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They combined for three straight 3-pointers after the Raptors led by six points

funFacts.text: Kyle Lowry nearly won the series with a buzzer-beating three, but Draymond Green deflected the shot.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Lowry's potential championship-winning, 3-point shot at the buzzer fell short
